name: Nina Arendt
life: “I still remember training a night nurse on the longest morning of my life.” People around Harbour Bakery know Nina by a small Sunday habit. Nina buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I trained her and missed every sign she was working past her limit.
appearance: Out of work clothes, look for a charcoal zip cardigan and a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. Nina has a long face and high cheekbones, with short copper curls. Nina draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Nina has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To ask the nurse which signs the educator missed.
family: Penelope Tang is Nina’s younger cousin. Nina remembers the birthdays. Penelope asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The first delivery fee*, Penelope says, “I volunteered because the route got me out of a miserable house.”
connections: Ashley Brooks (mentee). The educator lets the new nurse discuss the promotion without calling the former nurse replaceable.

reactions.situation: A replacement nurse receives the permanent badge
reactions.response: Nina welcomes the new nurse and saves the old worker's goodbye for a separate conversation.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Nina asks the counter staff for a receipt so its return can be traced even after their shift changes.

reactions.situation: When somebody trades on a title
reactions.response: Nina asks for the name of the person who will still be around tomorrow.
